scope.heading: Creation and Covenant
items: Genesis 1, Creation imago Dei and the sanctity of life

flashcard_sets.title: Genesis, Hannah and reading the Bible

flashcards.back: Latin for 'image of God'. Catholics believe every human is made in the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:27).
The worth every human person has because they are made in God's image. It can never be taken away or lost.
A human being made by God, with a body and a soul. A person can think, choose and love.
Humans are made to live in relationship with God and with other people. Genesis 2 says it is not good for the man to be alone.
Humans can think, reason and understand. This is part of being made in God's image.
Humans have free will. We can choose to do good or to do wrong.
The belief that all human life is sacred (holy) because it is a gift from God. Life must be protected from conception to natural death.
A lifelong, faithful union between a man and a woman, open to having children.
The sacrament where a baptised man and woman make vows before God to love each other faithfully for life. The couple give the sacrament to each other.
Reading the Old Testament to find people and events that point forward to Jesus and the New Testament.
Means 'first Gospel'. In Genesis 3:15 God promises that the woman's offspring will defeat the serpent. Catholics see this as the first promise of a Saviour.
The mother of Jesus. Catholics honour her as the greatest of all the saints.
A title for Mary. Jesus is truly God, so Mary, his mother, is the Mother of God.
The belief that Mary was kept free from original sin from the very start of her life, by God's grace. It is not the same as the Virgin Birth.
A title of love and respect that Catholics use for Mary.
A title for Mary. Eve said no to God. Mary said yes. Mary's obedience helps to undo Eve's disobedience.
Mary's song of praise to God in Luke 1, when she visits Elizabeth. It begins: 'My soul magnifies the Lord.'
A Catholic prayer using beads. People pray the Hail Mary and think about events in the lives of Jesus and Mary, called the mysteries.
The first creation story. God creates the world in six days and rests on the seventh. Humans are made last, male and female, in God's image. God sees it is very good.
The second creation story. God forms Adam from the dust and breathes life into him. God makes Eve as a partner for Adam. It focuses on relationships.
A sacred agreement or promise between God and his people.
Looking for a deeper, symbolic meaning in a Bible story, not only the literal meaning. Catholics do not have to read Genesis as a scientific account.
Believing a Bible story happened exactly as it is written, word for word.
A woman in 1 Samuel who could not have children. She prayed at the temple and promised to give her son to God. God answered her prayer and she had Samuel.
She shows faithful prayer and trust in God. Her song of praise in 1 Samuel 2 is like Mary's Magnificat. Catholics see her as pointing forward to Mary.
Hannah's son. He grew up serving God in the temple and became a great prophet.
The duty God gives humans to look after the world he made.
A message from God, spoken by a prophet. It often points to what God will do in the future.
The garden where God placed Adam and Eve in Genesis 2. Adam was given the job of looking after it.
A special sign through which Catholics believe God gives his grace. There are seven sacraments.
Genesis 2:24 says a husband and wife become one flesh. It shows that marriage is a deep, lifelong union.

quiz.q: What does 'Imago Dei' mean?
quiz.explain: Imago Dei is Latin for 'image of God'.

quiz.q: Which part of the Bible says humans are made in God's image?
quiz.explain: Genesis 1:27 says God created humans in his own image, male and female.

quiz.q: What does 'sanctity of life' mean?
options: Life is sacred because it comes from God
quiz.explain: Sanctity of life means all human life is holy because it is God's gift.

quiz.q: What does 'volitional' mean?
quiz.explain: Volitional means having free will, so we can choose.

quiz.q: What does 'rational' mean?
quiz.explain: Rational means humans can think, reason and understand.

quiz.q: In which creation story does God make Eve as a partner for Adam?
quiz.explain: Genesis 2 tells the story of Adam and Eve and focuses on relationships.

quiz.q: Genesis 1 says God created the world in how many days, before resting?
quiz.explain: God creates in six days and rests on the seventh day.

quiz.q: What does 'inalienable dignity' mean?
options: Dignity you earn by working hard
Worth that can never be taken away
quiz.explain: Every person has dignity because they are made in God's image, and it cannot be lost.

quiz.q: In the Sacrament of Matrimony, who gives the sacrament?
options: The bride and groom give it to each other
quiz.explain: In Catholic teaching the couple are the ministers of the sacrament. The priest or deacon is the Church's witness.

quiz.q: Which of these is part of Catholic teaching about marriage?
options: It lasts until one person wants to leave
It is lifelong, faithful and open to children
It is only a legal contract
It does not need any promises
quiz.explain: Catholics believe marriage is lifelong, faithful and open to new life.

quiz.q: What does 'relational' mean?
options: Humans are made to live alone
Humans are made for relationships with God and others
quiz.explain: Humans are made to be in relationship with God and with each other.

quiz.q: What does 'reading the Bible allegorically' mean?
options: Looking for a deeper, symbolic meaning
quiz.explain: An allegorical reading looks for deeper meaning beyond the literal story.

quiz.q: Who was Hannah's son?
quiz.explain: Hannah prayed for a child and God gave her Samuel.

quiz.q: Why do Catholics see a link between Hannah and Mary?
options: Both sang a song of praise to God about their child
quiz.explain: Hannah's song in 1 Samuel 2 is like Mary's Magnificat in Luke 1.

quiz.q: What is the Immaculate Conception?
options: Mary being taken up to heaven
Mary being free from original sin from the start of her life
quiz.explain: The Immaculate Conception is about Mary, not about Jesus' birth.

quiz.q: What does 'Protoevangelium' mean?
quiz.explain: Protoevangelium means 'first Gospel'. It refers to Genesis 3:15.

quiz.q: Why is Mary called the 'New Eve'?
options: She said yes to God where Eve said no
quiz.explain: Mary's obedience to God is compared with Eve's disobedience.

quiz.q: What is the Magnificat?
options: Mary's song of praise in Luke 1
The first book of the Bible
quiz.explain: The Magnificat begins 'My soul magnifies the Lord'.

quiz.q: What is typology?
options: Finding Old Testament people and events that point to Jesus
quiz.explain: Typology links Old Testament people and events to the New Testament.

quiz.q: What do people use to help them pray the Rosary?
quiz.explain: The Rosary uses beads to count the prayers.

quiz.q: In Genesis 2, what does God make Adam from?
quiz.explain: God forms Adam from the dust and breathes life into him.

quiz.q: Why does God make Eve in Genesis 2?
options: Because it is not good for the man to be alone
quiz.explain: God makes Eve as a partner, because humans are made for relationships.

quiz.q: What is stewardship?
options: The duty to look after God's world
quiz.explain: God gives humans the job of caring for creation.

quiz.q: How many sacraments are there in the Catholic Church?
quiz.explain: There are seven sacraments. Matrimony is one of them.

quiz.q: Genesis 2:24 says a husband and wife become…
quiz.explain: Catholics see 'one flesh' as God's plan for marriage.

quiz.q: Do Catholics have to read Genesis as a scientific account?
options: No, it teaches truths about God and people
quiz.explain: Catholics can read Genesis allegorically, for its deeper meaning.

quiz.q: Where did Hannah pray for a child?
quiz.explain: Hannah prayed at the temple and made a promise to God.

quiz.q: What did Hannah promise God?
options: That her son would serve God
quiz.explain: She promised her son would serve God, and she kept her promise.

quiz.q: Why is Mary called the Mother of God?
options: Her son Jesus is truly God
quiz.explain: Jesus is truly God, so his mother is the Mother of God.

writing_intro: Use a PEE paragraph: Point, Evidence, Explain. The first three are the Challenge questions from page 10. The last three are the Extended writing topics from page 10.

PEE.P: Make one clear point that answers the question.
PEE.E: Give evidence: a Bible quote, a Church teaching or an example.
PEE.X: Explain what the evidence shows and how it links to your point.

rag_topics.label: Genesis 1, Creation imago Dei and the sanctity of life

learn.title: Genesis 1
learn.text: Genesis 1 is the first creation story. God makes the world in six days and rests on the seventh. Humans are made last, male and female, and God calls creation very good.

learn.title: Imago Dei
learn.text: Genesis 1:27 says God made humans in his own image. Catholics call this imago Dei. Every person shares something of God: they can think, choose and love.

learn.title: Sanctity of life
learn.text: Because every person is made in God's image, Catholics believe all human life is sacred. Every person has a dignity that can never be taken away, from conception to natural death.

learn.title: Genesis 2
learn.text: The second creation story. God forms Adam from the dust of the ground and breathes life into him. He puts Adam in the Garden of Eden to look after it.

learn.title: Made for relationships
learn.text: God says it is not good for the man to be alone, so he makes Eve as a partner. Catholics learn from this that humans are made to live in relationship with God and with each other.

learn.title: Morality
learn.text: God gives Adam one rule: do not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Humans have free will, so they must choose how to act. Choosing what is right is morality.

learn.title: What is a sacrament?
learn.text: A sacrament is a special sign through which Catholics believe God gives his grace. There are seven sacraments. Matrimony (marriage) is one of them.

learn.title: Matrimony
learn.text: A baptised man and woman make vows before God. They promise to be faithful to each other for life and to be open to having children. The couple give the sacrament to each other.

learn.title: The link to Genesis 2
learn.text: Genesis 2:24 says a man and his wife become 'one flesh'. Catholics see this as God's plan for marriage from the very beginning.

learn.title: Literal and allegorical
learn.text: A literal reading takes a story word for word. An allegorical reading looks for a deeper meaning. Catholics do not have to read Genesis as a science report. It teaches truths about God and people.

learn.title: Typology
learn.text: Typology means finding people and events in the Old Testament that point forward to Jesus. For example, Catholics call Jesus the 'new Adam'.

learn.title: Protoevangelium
learn.text: In Genesis 3:15 God tells the serpent that the woman's offspring will crush its head. Catholics call this the Protoevangelium, or 'first Gospel', because it is the first promise of a Saviour.

learn.title: Who was Hannah?
learn.text: Her story is in 1 Samuel. Hannah could not have children and was very upset. She prayed at the temple and promised that if God gave her a son, he would serve God.

learn.title: God answers
learn.text: God answered her prayer and she had a son, Samuel. Hannah kept her promise and brought him to the temple. Samuel grew up to be a great prophet.

learn.title: Why Hannah matters
learn.text: Hannah shows faithful prayer and trust in God. After Samuel was born she sang a song of praise. Mary's Magnificat is very like it, so Catholics see Hannah as pointing forward to Mary.

learn.title: Mary
learn.text: Mary is the mother of Jesus. Catholics honour her more than any other saint. She has many titles, and each one says something about her.

learn.title: Mother of God and New Eve
learn.text: Jesus is truly God, so Mary is the Mother of God. She is also called the New Eve. Eve said no to God, but Mary said yes when the angel Gabriel came to her.

learn.title: Immaculate Conception
learn.text: Catholics believe Mary was kept free from original sin from the start of her life. This is the Immaculate Conception. It is about Mary's conception, not about Jesus' birth.

learn.title: Praying with Mary
learn.text: The Magnificat is the song of praise Mary sings in Luke 1. The Rosary is a prayer said with beads while thinking about events in the lives of Jesus and Mary.
